- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, cap peak forecast at 10–15% below true peak or use moving average to smooth.
- In absence of strong sentiment, model often underestimates mean-reversion trend; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for lagged mean reversion.
- When sentiment turns sharply positive (e.g., 1.00) and model fails to catch momentum, adjust forecast upward by 1–2% for next 3–5 periods.
- If model consistently underestimates late-period (last 5–7 days) prices, apply a 1–2% upward bias to final 5–7 forecast points.
- For sentiment history with alternating highs/lows, model often misjudges direction; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 3–5 days to anchor forecast.
